authors: The direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the standard of care for treatment and prevention of pulmonary embolism (PE) and deep venous thrombosis (DVT); also used for stroke prevention in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Ischemic strokes and cerebrovascular diseases often lead to symptomatic epilepsy among elderly patients; requiring addition of chronic antiepileptic drugs. The cytochrome P-450 (CYP 450) system is responsible for DOAC metabolism; while phenytoin is a well-documented CYP-450 inducer. We present a case with documented interaction between Apixaban and phenytoin; resulting in recurrent DVT.
